title: Unveiling Privacy Vulnerabilities: Investigating the Role of Structure in Graph Data

problem.claim: Adversaries may infer private user data from exposed network structure, including indirect structural patterns.

gap.claim: Prior privacy-leakage studies often focus on public user attributes and neglect privacy threats from exposed user relationships and network structure.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Generalized Homophily Ratio to quantify mechanisms contributing to graph privacy leakage via structure.
Develops a graph private attribute inference attack for evaluating privacy leakage through network structures under worst-case scenarios.
Proposes a graph data publishing method using learnable graph sampling to produce a privacy-preserving graph.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the Generalized Homophily Ratio, graph private attribute inference attack, and learnable graph sampling publishing method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their attack model poses a significant threat to user privacy.
The authors report that their graph data publishing method achieves the optimal privacy-utility trade-off compared with baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Exposed user information can enable privacy breaches and malicious activities.
Privacy risks from user relationships and network structure receive less attention than risks from public attributes.
The study investigates graph privacy leakage via structure and introduces a measure for its contributing mechanisms.
An inference attack evaluates structural privacy leakage under worst-case scenarios.
A learnable graph sampling publishing method is proposed, with experiments reporting privacy threats and privacy-utility performance.

unknowns: Datasets, experimental settings, and baseline identities are unspecified.
The definition and computation of the Generalized Homophily Ratio are unspecified.
Attack and graph sampling implementation details are unspecified.
Quantitative privacy and utility results are unspecified.
